comments.body:
Per the Turtle spec, """-escaped literals can contain any characters (including line breaks, carriage returns, etc.), other than """:

http://www.w3.org/TR/turtle/#h4_turtle-literals

I did some testing of this and found that RDF/XML can successfully include values with linebreaks, e.g.:

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<rdf:RDF xmlns:rdf="http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#"
xmlns:dcterms="http://purl.org/dc/terms/">
<rdf:Description rdf:about="http://localhost:8080/fcrepo4/rest/foo">
<dcterms:title>Test title value

with linebreaks</dcterms:title>
</rdf:Description>
</rdf:RDF>

The output in Turtle then include the value, with """-escaping. So I don't think the issue is that Jena lacks support for """-escaping since it's using it in the output.
Former user, what is your recommended approach for resolution here? to dig into the issue at the Jena level?

Since there is clearly support for """-escaping in Jena, I think we should first do the groundwork to see what the requirements are for Jena to parse them, and see if we can adjust how we use the Jena API for how we are reading in the Turtle. If we can't, then digging into the Jena parsing to figure out why it's failing would be the next step.

I'm unable to reproduce this using the REST API (assuming I'm understanding the concern correctly). It looks like the above example, i.e., the one with the triple quotes, is working OK.

I successfully created a container using the following:

curl -i -X POST -H "Content-Type: text/turtle" --data-binary "@body.rdf" "http://localhost:8080/rest"

<> <http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/title> """ """ .

And the following:

<> <http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/title> """this thing "rocks" the world""".

I just retried my tests, and I think I had an error in my local script. I updated my script and was able to POST turtle with """-escaped literals without any problems.

But justin and Adam Wead originally reported this issue, so I wonder whether something has changed to fix this, or if their case is failing still.
The original case we had included a CR-LF in the quotes. Has that been tested?

Yes, I can POST turtle with CRLF in the value:

curl -i -X POST -H "Content-Type: text/turtle" --data-binary "<> <http://purl.org/dc/terms/title> \"\"\"test with\r\nCRLF\"\"\" ." "http://localhost:8080/fcrepo4/rest"

When I retrieve the object that's created the CR and LF are present in the title value.

justin? Adam Wead? can you confirm/deny that this issue still exists?
This ticket will be closed as "Unable to reproduce" by April 20 unless we hear otherwise.

I can reproduce the issue via a spec in sufia if that is at all helpful: https://github.com/projecthydra/sufia/compare/master...psu-stewardship:ldp_error

This is the output of the spec
1) GenericFile complex description sound not raise ldp error
Failure/Error: subject.save!
Ldp::BadRequest:
RDF was not parsable: [line: 8, col: 1 ] Broken token (newline): ;

  1. ./spec/models/generic_file_spec.rb:624:in `block (3 levels) in <top (required)>'
Former user? Osman Din?

I think the issue here is that """-escaped literals work, but the value inside cannot end with a ". If I translate the value in that test to a curl command, I get:

curl -i -X POST -H "Content-Type: text/turtle" --data-binary "<> <http://purl.org/dc/terms/description> \"\"\"Data for:\r\nJournal: Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth\r\n\r\nArticle title: \"On the Origin and Evolution of Electrical Signals During Frictional Stick-Slip in Sheared Granular Material\"\"\"\"" "http://localhost:8080/fcrepo4/rest"

This fails because it ends with four " symbols in a row. The first three are interepreted as the end of the quote, and the final " produces the error. If I add a space after the value and before the """-terminator, then it works:

curl -i -X POST -H "Content-Type: text/turtle" --data-binary "<> <http://purl.org/dc/terms/description> \"\"\"Data for:\r\nJournal: Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth\r\n\r\nArticle title: \"On the Origin and Evolution of Electrical Signals During Frictional Stick-Slip in Sheared Granular Material\" \"\"\"" "http://localhost:8080/fcrepo4/rest"

It will also work if I backslash-escape the quotes:

curl -i -X POST -H "Content-Type: text/turtle" --data-binary "<> <http://purl.org/dc/terms/description> \"\"\"Data for:\r\nJournal: Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth\r\n\r\nArticle title: \\\"On the Origin and Evolution of Electrical Signals During Frictional Stick-Slip in Sheared Granular Material\\\"\"\"\"" "http://localhost:8080/fcrepo4/rest"
Any news on this ticket? Is it still an issue? Can you update the status Esmé Cowles, and close if necessary.

Closing as Can't Reproduce – the only instance of this bug that I was able to verify was when a """-escaped literal ended with a quote – which produced four quotes in a row, which I don't think is valid.
